newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed at highs after a quiet day in which investors braced for important U.S. jobs data on Friday that could signal interest rate hikes there.

Guilder bonds benefited from paper scarcity, especially in 10-year debt which end-investors such as pension funds use to cover obligations. The Dutch state, the biggest guilder issuer, has borrowed no 10-year debt this year. Scarcity prompted the discount of Dutch to German paper to widen to 11 basis points.
Also, recovering economic growth -- Dutch GDP rose 2.3 percent y/y in the first half year -- will increase taxes and reduce the state's borrowing requirements, one dealer said.
Meanwhile, absence of inflation fears left the long end of the market unharmed, they say.

"Strong growth used to trigger inflation fears, but tight government budgets and wage restraint have calmed people down. These days higher growth just means: more tax income, less state borrowing and scarcer paper," one trader said.

The German economy showed a surprise sign of recovery when second quarter GDP data were published this morning, growing 1.2 percent y/y. But higher unemployment dampened the negative impact on bonds. The short end of the curve looked marginally weaker than the longer end.

"The short end has done well recently because people can still find very cheap money in the money market, but more rate cuts now seem unnecessary and that will take momentum out of notes," a trader said.

The 30-year bond was lagging behind 10-year paper for more technical reasons, as the long German bond was sold while investors were not keen to switch to Dutch 2024s which they regard much too expensive at 19 basis points under Germany.
